audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity may be operating cash encumbered by customer obligations
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $84.28 million cash and short-term investments; computed maximum effect $1.90 per share, equal to 6.2% of base equity value; filed contract liabilities $174.78 million and net contract liability $116.755 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash to equity value even though some cash may finance contract performance obligations already reflected in forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities consist of advance payments and billings in excess of costs incurred and deferred revenue, and represent amounts received in excess of sales recognized on contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification issue, not a demonstrated $84.28 million error. Nevertheless, contract liabilities exceed the cash addition, and removing the entire addition would reduce base value from $30.46 to about $28.56 per share and the buy-below price from $21.32 to about $19.99. That range is reasonably capable of affecting the valuation threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash and investments to restricted balances, customer advances, contract assets, minimum operating liquidity, and near-term contract costs; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Vidrio Andino may be counted both in owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $51.7 million stakes addition and filed 2025 equity-method income of $2.493 million in the income statement or $2.658 million in the investment note; computed base capitalized effect approximately $35.0-$37.3 million if that income remains in anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income may be capitalized through owner earnings while the affiliate investment is separately added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Income from this investment is recorded using the equity method and is presented within the Consolidated Statement of Operations as a component of non-operating income as the Company is not subject to income tax over this investment.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method income enters net income, but the supplied record does not show whether it was removed from owner earnings. A correction could reduce base value by roughly $0.79-$0.84 per share through the OE route, or by $1.17 per share if the entire stakes addition were removed. The missing reconciliation prevents establishing which amount, if any, is duplicated and whether the stakes balance contains other assets.
audit_findings.action: Provide the year-by-year OE reconciliation identifying equity-method income and dividends, reconcile the $51.7 million stakes balance to Vidrio Andino and other investments, then rerun with either affiliate earnings or affiliate value—but not both.

audit_findings.title: The forecast interest burden may not match the higher 2026 debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed June 2026 debt $225.394 million; filed six-month 2026 financing cost $6.543 million versus full-year 2025 $3.445 million; computed annualized difference $9.641 million and base-value effect about $135.4 million or $3.05 per share before tax normalization
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted, current and continuing interest expense must reduce equity-level owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded a gain of $3.3 million related to derivative financial instruments.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher financing burden is demonstrated in the 2026 interim results: six-month financing cost already exceeds the entire 2025 amount. Annualizing the interim line would reduce the base operating valuation by about 10%, which is material to the stated value and buy-below threshold. The precise sustainable amount remains unresolved because derivative effects, deferred financing costs, debt timing, taxes, and the November 2026 hedge expiry require normalization.
audit_findings.action: Build a current debt schedule using principal balances, SOFR plus contractual spreads, the $110 million hedge through November 2026, and post-expiry rates; exclude fair-value gains and losses, apply the appropriate tax effect, and rerun all scenarios from normalized equity-level OE.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain nonrecurring aircraft and government-credit gains
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $5.641 million pretax other operating income, equal to 6.5% of the $86.5 million anchor; computed maximum base-value effect about $79.2 million or $1.79 per share before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring operating gains increase the anchor OE and are then capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded other operating income of $5.6 million mainly related to a gain on the sale of an aircraft and the recognition of a refund related to Employee Retention Credits under government relief programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their inclusion in OE is unresolved because no anchor reconciliation was supplied. If retained dollar-for-dollar, they would produce a roughly 5.9% overstatement of base equity value and reduce the reliability of an already volatile anchor. That is reasonably capable of affecting the valuation threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE to net income and show separate removal of the aircraft-sale gain and Employee Retention Credit refund with their actual tax effects; rerun every scenario if either remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: A newly formed 60%-owned entity creates a possible unrecognized NCI claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $0.901 million investment; computed implied 40% outside interest approximately $0.601 million or $0.014 per share if ownership economics are proportional
audit_findings.mechanism: If Storm Armour Solutions were consolidated, earnings attributable to its 40% outside owners would need removal from OE and any NCI claim would enter the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Tecnoglass Armour, LLC has a 60 % of the capital contribution of Storm Armour Solutions, LLC.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing records a $0.901 million investment and does not present a noncontrolling-interest balance, indicating that Storm Armour Solutions is not currently contributing consolidated economics requiring a 40% allocation. Even treating the omitted outside interest as $0.601 million would equal about 0.04% of base equity value and cannot materially affect the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the accounting classification and identify any Storm Armour income included in consolidated OE; revisit only if later filings consolidate the entity or its earnings become significant.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial year of the acquired Contiglass business
audit_findings.magnitude: filed nine-month revenue $14.5 million and loss $2.7 million; filed pro forma 2025 net income $157.452 million versus actual $159.566 million, a computed decrease of $2.114 million or 2.4% of the OE anchor; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A perimeter adjustment would alter anchor OE for the missing pre-acquisition period and could also separate continuing earnings from acquisition and integration costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Contiglass Asset Acquisition, LLC, contributed revenues of $ 14.5 million and a loss of $ 2.7 million to The Company for the period from April 3, 2025, to December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year perimeter issue is demonstrated, but the filed full-year pro forma comparison changes net income by only $2.114 million. If that difference flowed dollar-for-dollar into OE, the computed base-value effect would be about $29.7 million or $0.67 per share, approximately 2.2% of base equity value and insufficient to change the present valuation conclusion. Future integration gains or continuing losses are not established by this historical comparison.
audit_findings.action: Compare the anchor with Contiglass full-year pro forma OE and 2026 run-rate OE, separately identifying acquisition costs, integration costs, maintenance capex, and working-capital requirements; monitor and rerun if continuing OE departs materially from the filed pro forma scale.
